Ifmyante wrote:

IF, this is a nice explanation. I have just a
question about your thinking proces. Can you please tell me if this was
the reason for you?

Why you didn't marked end of CP where my blue line is?

And this is my answer. CP was ended there and price made a FL (the blue
one). After that price tested that FL (you see it tested the MPL of it)
it made another FL (the green one). Since the blue one was taken out,
the green one its the valid target for that PAZ. So, you can short the
source of the move down which is in the green FL. After price hit the
green FL (source of the move down) It made another FL (the brown one).
So the source of the brown FL can be shorted.

And now, the targets.

Thank you so much IF! :)

author: Ifmyante
text:
Whenever I post here, I get messages asking will we be opening the academy again.

I have no definitive answer to that, I'm afraid.

It seems that teaching everything I know has a great effect on some
students' trading in a short time, but for others it takes years, or may
 not happen at all.

We're all so different, that some make absolutely perfect entries and
exits, while others' trades seem utterly arbitrary, like they've never
been taught anything at all!

When I retell a lesson, it's often received as if I'd never told it before, and it seems to be soon forgotten again!

So far, I estimate that only between 20-30% of students have really
gotten it. I know the rest can get it too, but they'll need to exorcise
their demons in order to succeed.

So, to answer those messages:

You're welcome to apply for a place in the academy if

you're ready to put between six months and three years into transforming nurture into nature

you can usually retain lessons you've been taught

you can already adhere to strict money management rules

your loved ones will give you the time to do this, without putting pressure on you to succeed

I'll interview each applicant in due course, to assess (hopefully
correctly!) whether they have a good chance of success, and if we get
enough applicants with the right stuff, I may open the doors again. It'd
 be great to have some new voices in the trading room

author: Ifmyante
text:
I strongly suggest avoiding moving stop to BE. It's the easiest way to be taken out of great trades.

It's far better to take enough profit at tg1 to cover your original stop
 being hit. Then you can't lose, and don't get knocked out of runners

author: Ifmyante
text:
Ahmadhassan745 wrote: Thanks IF for giving good suggestions.

I read in a book, which is designed by FX Sniffer. In this book, there
is an interview from a trader. He said to avoid using exact SL. He
suggest to use Virtual Stop Loss. What you think about placing SL???

We absolutely must have an hard stop, always.

But if we don't have an engulf before entry, we don't put it directly
above the high or below the low, where all the retail stops lie.

Instead, we find a lovely LTF RBD/DBR just beyond, and put it on the
other side of that, so that we have the best chance to get out at BE or
in big profit from the usual RT

Muffler do you mind elaborating why you see that as QM level? For my
understanding QM happens when uptrend (HL HH HL HH) gets engulfed by LL
or downtrend (LH LL LH LL) gets engulfed by HH. After this happens we
wait for it to retrace back to DP where engulf happened and play QM
setup or H & S setup they both are same set up but just different
names.

As for what I see as significant would be on the left where strong move
down happened. I would mark ftr/FL on spaces within that down move

 of it.

section of chart? The pole, subsequent flag and then continuation south,
 implying that it was an important engulf south and new FTR?

I've noticed that when a pole/LQ push breaks a previously important
level, the top (if bullish)/bottom (if bearish) end of the impulse that
breaks the level subsequently becomes a key PAZ boundary.
